{"id":"src:D01","kind":"adr","title":"D01-cap-file-uploads-at-10-mb","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D01-cap-file-uploads-at-10-mb.md","text":"# ADR D01: Cap file uploads at 10 MB

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-02-10
- Owner: Ada Okafor (Platform lead)
- Systems: uploads-api

## Context

Support has been fielding failed uploads for weeks. The failures are confusing because the request looks accepted and then dies somewhere behind the edge: All file uploads pass through the API gateway, so anything over the gateway's limit is dropped with a bare 413 and no application error. Rather than chase each report we want one clear rule at the API.

Stated premises:

- All file uploads pass through the API gateway. (fact)
  This holds because the API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit.

## Decision

Reject any upload over 10 MB at the API with a clear error instead of letting it fail downstream.

## Alternatives considered

- Stream uploads directly to S3 with presigned URLs (rejected: two weeks of work for a problem we can rule out today)
- Raise the gateway limit (rejected: the platform team owns Envoy and does not want per-route exceptions)

## Consequences

The uploads API returns a 413 with a readable message at 10 MB. The mobile and web clients should check size before sending. If the gateway limit ever changes this cap should be revisited, because it exists only to mirror it.
"}

{"id":"src:D02","kind":"adr","title":"D02-chunk-csv-imports-into-5-mb-parts","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D02-chunk-csv-imports-into-5-mb-parts.md","text":"# ADR D02: Chunk CSV imports into 5 MB parts

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-03-01
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (Backend engineer)
- Systems: data-pipeline

## Context

Customer CSV imports regularly run to 40 or 50 MB. The API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit, so a single request cannot carry them. We do not want to run a separate ingestion endpoint outside the gateway.

Stated premises:

- The API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit. (constraint)

## Decision

Split customer CSV imports client-side into 5 MB parts and reassemble them in the pipeline.

## Alternatives considered

- SFTP drop (rejected: customers hate it and support hates it more)
- Compress before upload (rejected: still over the limit for the large accounts)

## Consequences

The import client splits files into 5 MB parts with a manifest; the pipeline reassembles and validates row counts. Partial imports are retried per part.
"}

{"id":"src:D03","kind":"adr","title":"D03-reject-photos-over-8-mb-in-the-mobile-app","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D03-reject-photos-over-8-mb-in-the-mobile-app.md","text":"# ADR D03: Reject photos over 8 MB in the mobile app

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-04-12
- Owner: Sofia Rossi (Frontend lead)
- Systems: mobile-app

## Context

Photos from recent phones are 12 to 20 MB. The API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit, and a rejected request on a mobile connection wastes the user's data and their patience. Rejecting on the device, with an explanation, is kinder than failing after the upload.

Stated premises:

- The API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit. (constraint)

## Decision

The mobile app refuses photos over 8 MB before upload and asks the user to pick a smaller one.

## Alternatives considered

- Downscale on device (deferred: the image pipeline team wants originals)
- Chunked upload (rejected: the mobile SDK does not support it)

## Consequences

Photos over 8 MB are refused in the picker with a message. The 8 MB number leaves headroom under the gateway limit for the multipart envelope.
"}

{"id":"src:D04","kind":"adr","title":"D04-rebuild-the-search-index-in-full-every-night","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D04-rebuild-the-search-index-in-full-every-night.md","text":"# ADR D04: Rebuild the search index in full every night

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-11-20
- Owner: Lena Fischer (Data engineer)
- Systems: search

## Context

The search index drifts from the database within hours because partial updates fail on the nested fields. Our Elasticsearch mapping cannot take incremental updates; the mapping change that would allow them is a multi-week migration nobody can staff this quarter.

Stated premises:

- Our Elasticsearch mapping cannot take incremental updates. (constraint)

## Decision

A nightly job drops and rebuilds the whole search index rather than applying updates.

## Alternatives considered

- Fix the mapping now (deferred to Q1)
- Dual-write with a reconciliation job (rejected: more moving parts than the problem deserves)

## Consequences

A nightly job at 02:00 UTC drops and rebuilds the index. Search results can be up to a day stale. Revisit when the mapping migration lands.
"}

{"id":"src:D05","kind":"adr","title":"D05-use-postgres-for-every-storage-need","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D05-use-postgres-for-every-storage-need.md","text":"# ADR D05: Use Postgres for every storage need

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-06-01
- Owner: Tomi Adeyemi (CTO)
- Systems: infra

## Context

We keep adding infrastructure. Every new datastore is another thing to back up, monitor, and explain to the auditor.

_No premise was recorded for this decision._

## Decision

No new datastore is introduced; queues, caches and documents all live in Postgres.

## Alternatives considered

- Redis for queues, S3 for documents (rejected)

## Consequences

Queues use SKIP LOCKED tables, caches are unlogged tables, documents are JSONB. Exceptions need a written ADR.
"}

{"id":"src:D06","kind":"adr","title":"D06-rotate-api-keys-every-90-days","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D06-rotate-api-keys-every-90-days.md","text":"# ADR D06: Rotate API keys every 90 days

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-01-15
- Owner: Jonah Mbeki (Security engineer)
- Systems: auth

## Context

The SOC 2 auditor requires credential rotation at most every 90 days. Our keys currently never expire, which came up as a finding in the readiness assessment.

Stated premises:

- The SOC 2 auditor requires credential rotation at most every 90 days. (constraint)
  This holds because we need SOC 2 certification to sell to enterprise customers.

## Decision

All service and customer API keys expire after 90 days and must be rotated.

## Alternatives considered

- Rotate on demand only (rejected: fails the control)

## Consequences

Keys carry an expiry; the auth service refuses expired keys; customers get a reminder at 14 and 3 days.
"}

{"id":"src:D07","kind":"adr","title":"D07-freeze-production-deploys-on-fridays","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D07-freeze-production-deploys-on-fridays.md","text":"# ADR D07: Freeze production deploys on Fridays

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-09-05
- Owner: Marcus Chen (SRE)
- Systems: infra

## Context

Two of the last three incidents started with a Friday afternoon deploy and ran into the weekend. A rollback requires a manual database restore, which takes the on-call engineer about forty minutes and needs a second person to verify. On a Friday evening that second person is often unreachable.

Stated premises:

- A rollback requires a manual database restore. (constraint)

## Decision

No production deploy from Friday 12:00 to Monday 09:00.

## Alternatives considered

- Deploy freeze only for schema changes (rejected: too hard to police)
- Automated rollback (deferred: needs the migration tooling first)

## Consequences

No production deploy from Friday 12:00 to Monday 09:00 local time. Hotfixes need the on-call lead's approval.
"}

{"id":"src:D08","kind":"adr","title":"D08-keep-the-monolith-no-new-services","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D08-keep-the-monolith-no-new-services.md","text":"# ADR D08: Keep the monolith; no new services

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-05-20
- Owner: Tomi Adeyemi (CTO)
- Systems: infra

## Context

There is a recurring proposal to extract the billing and notifications code into services. The engineering team is under 15 people. At that size the coordination cost of services (contracts, deploys, on-call surface) outweighs the autonomy they buy. The monolith's modules already have clear owners.

Stated premises:

- The engineering team is under 15 people. (fact)

## Decision

New features are built inside the monolith; service extraction proposals are declined.

## Alternatives considered

- Extract billing only (rejected: it is the most entangled module)
- Modular monolith with enforced boundaries (accepted as part of this decision)

## Consequences

New features go in the monolith. Extraction proposals are declined until the team is large enough that deploy contention is a measured problem.
"}

{"id":"src:D09","kind":"adr","title":"D09-serve-eu-customers-from-frankfurt-only","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D09-serve-eu-customers-from-frankfurt-only.md","text":"# ADR D09: Serve EU customers from Frankfurt only

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-07-01
- Owner: Ada Okafor (Platform lead)
- Systems: infra

- Supersedes: ADR D28

## Context

The EU data residency question comes up in every enterprise deal. All EU customers are in Germany and Austria, so one region in Frankfurt covers residency and keeps latency under 30 ms for every EU tenant we have.

Stated premises:

- All EU customers are in Germany and Austria. (fact)
  This holds because we sell to customers in the European Union.

## Decision

A single EU region in Frankfurt serves all EU tenants.

## Alternatives considered

- Frankfurt plus Paris (rejected: doubles the infrastructure cost for no current customer)
- EU tenants in us-east-1 with contractual promises (rejected by legal)

## Consequences

All EU tenants are provisioned in eu-central-1. A second EU region needs a new ADR.
"}

{"id":"src:D10","kind":"adr","title":"D10-send-notifications-through-sendgrid","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D10-send-notifications-through-sendgrid.md","text":"# ADR D10: Send notifications through SendGrid

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-08-10
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (Backend engineer)
- Systems: notifications

## Context

We send password resets, invoices and a weekly digest. Notification volume is under 100 emails a day, inside the SendGrid free tier. Building on the free plan means no procurement and no contract to review.

Stated premises:

- Notification volume is under 100 emails a day, inside the SendGrid free tier. (fact)
  This holds because tooling and infrastructure spend must stay under $20,000 a month.

## Decision

All transactional email goes through SendGrid on the free plan.

## Alternatives considered

- SES (rejected: deliverability setup took longer than the whole integration)

## Consequences

All transactional mail goes through SendGrid. Volume is reported monthly; the free tier is the budget.
"}

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-10-01
- Owner: Tomi Adeyemi (CTO)
- Systems: infra

## Context

Bugs are reaching production that a second pair of eyes would have caught. CI runs no automated test suite; until it does, review is the only gate we have.

Stated premises:

- CI runs no automated test suite. (fact)

## Decision

Every PR needs two approvals before merge.

## Alternatives considered

- One reviewer plus a checklist (rejected: the checklist was being rubber-stamped)

## Consequences

Branch protection requires two approvals. Expect slower merges; pair on reviews to keep the queue short.
"}

{"id":"src:D12","kind":"adr","title":"D12-store-sessions-in-redis","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D12-store-sessions-in-redis.md","text":"# ADR D12: Store sessions in Redis

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-07-15
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (Backend engineer)
- Systems: auth

## Context

The web tier must stay stateless so it can autoscale. Sticky sessions on the load balancer kept biting us during deploys, when an instance drained and its users were logged out.

Stated premises:

- The web tier must stay stateless so it can autoscale. (constraint)

## Decision

Web sessions live in Redis, never in process memory.

## Alternatives considered

- Signed cookies only (rejected: we need server-side revocation)

## Consequences

Sessions live in Redis with a 30-day TTL. Any instance can serve any request; deploys no longer log users out.
"}

{"id":"src:D13","kind":"adr","title":"D13-encrypt-pii-in-the-application-layer","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D13-encrypt-pii-in-the-application-layer.md","text":"# ADR D13: Encrypt PII in the application layer

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-02-01
- Owner: Jonah Mbeki (Security engineer)
- Systems: billing

## Context

Enterprise customers ask for encryption with keys we control. RDS does not support customer-managed encryption keys in eu-central-1, so database-level encryption cannot satisfy that today.

Stated premises:

- RDS does not support customer-managed encryption keys in eu-central-1. (constraint)

## Decision

PII columns are encrypted by the application with our own keys before they reach the database.

## Alternatives considered

- Move to a region where RDS supports CMK (rejected: residency)
- Wait for AWS (rejected: no date)

## Consequences

The application encrypts PII columns with per-tenant keys from KMS before writing. Searching on encrypted columns is not possible; design around it.
"}

{"id":"src:D14","kind":"adr","title":"D14-bill-in-usd-only","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D14-bill-in-usd-only.md","text":"# ADR D14: Bill in USD only

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-06-20
- Owner: Tomi Adeyemi (CTO)
- Systems: billing

## Context

Multi-currency billing is not enabled on our Stripe account. Enabling it means a new contract, tax reviews per currency, and reconciliation work finance is not staffed for.

Stated premises:

- Multi-currency billing is not enabled on our Stripe account. (fact)

## Decision

All invoices are issued in US dollars regardless of customer location.

## Alternatives considered

- Invoice in EUR for EU customers via a second Stripe account (rejected: two sets of books)

## Consequences

Every invoice is in USD. Sales should set expectations early in EU deals.
"}

{"id":"src:D15","kind":"adr","title":"D15-support-safari-15-and-newer-only","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D15-support-safari-15-and-newer-only.md","text":"# ADR D15: Support Safari 15 and newer only

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-03-15
- Owner: Sofia Rossi (Frontend lead)
- Systems: web-app

## Context

We carry a pile of polyfills and CSS workarounds for old Safari. Safari versions below 15 are under 1% of traffic, and the maintenance cost of those workarounds is measured in incidents, not in users.

Stated premises:

- Safari versions below 15 are under 1% of traffic. (fact)

## Decision

The web app drops polyfills and workarounds for Safari below version 15.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep supporting Safari 13 (rejected)

## Consequences

Polyfills for Safari below 15 are removed. The support page states the minimum version.
"}

{"id":"src:D16","kind":"adr","title":"D16-never-write-pii-to-logs","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D16-never-write-pii-to-logs.md","text":"# ADR D16: Never write PII to logs

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-09-01
- Owner: Jonah Mbeki (Security engineer)
- Systems: infra

## Context

GDPR applies to our EU users. A log line with an email address in it is personal data in a system with 30-day retention and broad read access.

Stated premises:

- GDPR applies to our EU users. (constraint)
  This holds because we sell to customers in the European Union.

## Decision

Log lines are scrubbed of personal data before shipping.

## Alternatives considered

- Restrict log access instead (rejected: does not address retention)

## Consequences

The logging library scrubs known PII fields; a CI check fails on new log calls that pass user objects.
"}

{"id":"src:D17","kind":"adr","title":"D17-use-launchdarkly-for-feature-flags","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D17-use-launchdarkly-for-feature-flags.md","text":"# ADR D17: Use LaunchDarkly for feature flags

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-06-10
- Owner: Marcus Chen (SRE)
- Systems: web-app

## Context

Our flag table has no audit log, no targeting rules and no kill switch UI. LaunchDarkly costs under $500 a month at our seat count, which is cheaper than the engineer-week a year we spend on the table.

Stated premises:

- LaunchDarkly costs under $500 a month at our seat count. (fact)
  This holds because tooling and infrastructure spend must stay under $20,000 a month.

## Decision

Feature flags are managed in LaunchDarkly rather than a home-grown table.

## Alternatives considered

- Unleash self-hosted (rejected: another service to run)
- Keep the table and add an admin UI (rejected: see cost)

## Consequences

Flags move to LaunchDarkly; the table is read-only until migrated. Revisit if the bill grows past the budget.
"}

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-11-01
- Owner: Sofia Rossi (Frontend lead)
- Systems: web-app

## Context

There is no end-to-end test coverage of the web app, so a release can break checkout without any test noticing. Until there is coverage, a person walks the checklist in staging.

Stated premises:

- There is no end-to-end test coverage of the web app. (fact)

## Decision

A person walks the release checklist in staging before each production release.

## Alternatives considered

- Ship behind flags and monitor (rejected: checkout cannot be flagged per user)

## Consequences

Every production release of the web app has a signed-off checklist in the release ticket. This is a stopgap; the end-to-end suite is the real fix.
"}

{"id":"src:D19","kind":"adr","title":"D19-run-the-data-pipeline-hourly-not-continuously","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D19-run-the-data-pipeline-hourly-not-continuously.md","text":"# ADR D19: Run the data pipeline hourly, not continuously

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-08-01
- Owner: Lena Fischer (Data engineer)
- Systems: data-pipeline

## Context

Running the pipeline continuously looked attractive for freshness, but Warehouse query cost scales with how often the pipeline runs, and our warehouse bill tripled in the month we tried it.

Stated premises:

- Warehouse query cost scales with how often the pipeline runs. (fact)
  This holds because we are on BigQuery on-demand pricing.

## Decision

The pipeline batches events and runs once an hour.

## Alternatives considered

- Micro-batches every 5 minutes (rejected: same cost shape)
- Streaming into a cheaper store (deferred)

## Consequences

The pipeline runs hourly. Dashboards can be up to an hour behind. Revisit if the warehouse pricing model changes.
"}

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-09-01
- Owner: Sofia Rossi (Frontend lead)
- Systems: mobile-app

## Context

React Native 0.74 defaults to the New Architecture. The payments SDK does not support the React Native New Architecture, and payments are the one part of the app we cannot ship without.

Stated premises:

- The payments SDK does not support the React Native New Architecture. (constraint)

## Decision

The mobile app stays on React Native 0.72 and the old architecture.

## Alternatives considered

- Fork the SDK (rejected: unmaintainable)
- Web checkout in a webview (rejected: conversion drop)

## Consequences

The app stays on 0.72 with the old architecture until the payments vendor ships support. Track their release notes.
"}

{"id":"src:D22","kind":"adr","title":"D22-review-access-grants-every-month","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D22-review-access-grants-every-month.md","text":"# ADR D22: Review access grants every month

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-04-01
- Owner: Jonah Mbeki (Security engineer)
- Systems: auth

## Context

The SOC 2 auditor requires credential rotation at most every 90 days, and the same control expects access to be reviewed. We currently review access when someone leaves, which the auditor flagged as insufficient.

Stated premises:

- The SOC 2 auditor requires credential rotation at most every 90 days. (constraint)
  This holds because we need SOC 2 certification to sell to enterprise customers.

## Decision

A monthly review removes stale access to production systems.

## Alternatives considered

- Quarterly review (rejected: fails the control)

## Consequences

A monthly ticket lists every production grant; owners confirm or revoke within a week.
"}

{"id":"src:D23","kind":"adr","title":"D23-use-uuidv4-for-every-primary-key","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D23-use-uuidv4-for-every-primary-key.md","text":"# ADR D23: Use UUIDv4 for every primary key

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-06-15
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (Backend engineer)
- Systems: infra

## Context

Serial integer keys collide the moment data moves between databases. We plan to shard Postgres by tenant, and merging per-tenant tables with overlapping integer ids would be a migration from hell.

Stated premises:

- We plan to shard Postgres by tenant. (assumption)

## Decision

Tables use UUIDv4 primary keys instead of serial integers.

## Alternatives considered

- Snowflake-style ids (rejected: needs a coordinator service)
- ULIDs (deferred: no library we trusted at the time)

## Consequences

Every new table uses UUIDv4 primary keys. Index bloat is accepted. Revisit if the sharding plan changes.
"}

{"id":"src:D24","kind":"adr","title":"D24-one-week-on-call-shifts","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D24-one-week-on-call-shifts.md","text":"# ADR D24: One-week on-call shifts

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-01-10
- Owner: Marcus Chen (SRE)
- Systems: infra

## Context

Only four engineers are trained for on-call. Shorter shifts would put each of them on call every other week, which is worse than one full week in four.

Stated premises:

- Only four engineers are trained for on-call. (fact)

## Decision

On-call rotates weekly among the trained engineers.

## Alternatives considered

- Follow-the-sun with contractors (rejected: cost)

## Consequences

Shifts run Monday to Monday. Training more engineers for on-call is the way to shorten them.
"}

{"id":"src:D25","kind":"adr","title":"D25-disable-public-sign-ups","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D25-disable-public-sign-ups.md","text":"# ADR D25: Disable public sign-ups

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-10-01
- Owner: Tomi Adeyemi (CTO)
- Systems: web-app

## Context

Free-tier bots are abusing public sign-up: last month 80% of new accounts were bots creating workspaces to host spam. Captchas slowed them for a week.

Stated premises:

- Free-tier bots are abusing public sign-up. (fact)

## Decision

New accounts are created only through sales; the public sign-up form is off.

## Alternatives considered

- Email verification plus rate limits (rejected: tried, bypassed)
- Paid-only sign-up (rejected: kills trials)

## Consequences

The sign-up form is disabled; sales creates accounts. Marketing is told conversion from the site will drop.
"}

- Systems: infra

## Context

Log storage costs about $0.50 per GB a month, and we were storing eighteen months of logs nobody read. The last three incidents used logs from the previous day.

Stated premises:

- Log storage costs about $0.50 per GB a month. (fact)
  This holds because tooling and infrastructure spend must stay under $20,000 a month.

## Decision

Application logs are deleted after 30 days.

## Alternatives considered

- 90 days (rejected: cost)
- Cold storage after 30 days (deferred)

## Consequences

Logs are deleted after 30 days. Security events are exported separately with longer retention.
"}

{"id":"src:D27","kind":"adr","title":"D27-manage-all-infrastructure-with-terraform","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D27-manage-all-infrastructure-with-terraform.md","text":"# ADR D27: Manage all infrastructure with Terraform

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2024-07-01
- Owner: Marcus Chen (SRE)
- Systems: infra

## Context

SOC 2 requires infrastructure to be reproducible from code. Resources created in the console cannot be shown to be reproducible, and we had drift between staging and production that nobody could explain.

Stated premises:

- SOC 2 requires infrastructure to be reproducible from code. (constraint)
  This holds because we need SOC 2 certification to sell to enterprise customers.

## Decision

No cloud resource is created by hand; everything goes through Terraform.

## Alternatives considered

- CloudFormation (rejected: the team knows Terraform)

## Consequences

No console changes. Every resource is in Terraform with a reviewed plan. Break-glass changes are reverted into code within a day.
"}

{"id":"src:D30","kind":"adr","title":"D30-block-third-party-cookies-in-the-embed-widget","date":null,"author":null,"path":"corpus/adr/D30-block-third-party-cookies-in-the-embed-widget.md","text":"# ADR D30: Block third-party cookies in the embed widget

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2025-11-05
- Owner: Sofia Rossi (Frontend lead)
- Systems: web-app

## Context

Chrome will remove third-party cookies in 2025. The embed widget relies on a third-party cookie to keep users signed in across customer sites, and that will simply stop working.

Stated premises:

- Chrome will remove third-party cookies in 2025. (assumption)

## Decision

The embeddable widget uses first-party storage only.

## Alternatives considered

- Storage Access API prompts (rejected: too many prompts per session)

## Consequences

The widget uses first-party storage with a short-lived token exchange. Expect more sign-in prompts on customer sites.
"}
